Overview

Yatri Hub is a smart companion app for Yatri electric bike riders, offering real-time bike monitoring, ride history, and quick access to essential stats.

It enhances the user experience by providing features like nearby charging station locations, navigation routes, and seamless connectivity, promoting a sustainable and connected lifestyle.

YATRI MOTORCYCLES

The Problem We Chose to Solve

Owning an electric bike introduces a new kind of uncertainty. Riders often don’t know:

  • How their vehicle is performing,
  • Whether their battery and range are reliable,
  • How to interpret ride and charging data over time.

While the scooter hardware provided rich telemetry, riders lacked a clear, trustworthy interface to understand and act on that information. This led to confusion, frequent support questions, and reduced confidence in everyday use.

This project focused on designing Yatri Hub, a mobile product that becomes the rider’s primary way to understand, manage, and trust their vehicle.

Product Goals

The goal was not just to build an app, but to improve the post-purchase ownership experience.

Primary Goals

  • Increase rider confidence and sense of control
  • Reduce ambiguity around charging, range, and performance
  • Encourage consistent engagement beyond initial ownership

What Success Looked Like

  • App activation after vehicle delivery
  • Weekly active usage among riders
  • Engagement with ride summaries and vehicle status
  • Reduction in support questions related to vehicle status

My Role & Scope

I worked as the primary product designer, owning the experience end to end:

  • Framing the problem and defining success
  • Synthesizing user research into product decisions
  • Designing system architecture, interactions, and UI
  • Collaborating closely with engineering and product

User Stories

  • As a new electric bike owner, I want an easy-to-use interface that clearly displays essential metrics, so can understand my bike’s performance at a glance.
  • I want the app to notify me when my bike needs charging or has an issue so that I can address it without delay.
  • As someone who loves long rides, I want a feature that tracks my journey and provides stats.

After surveys and in-depth interviews, I discovered 2 common themes in our users

Key Insights

Design opportunities

Users want to use an integrated app with real-time monitoring and remote control features

Develop integrated features like remote locking/unlocking, geo-fencing, and real-time notifications

Users want to know nearby charging stations and their bike’s reachable range on the map

Trade-offs & Constraints

  • Advanced customization was intentionally deferred to keep onboarding simple
  • Some features were redesigned to align with hardware telemetry limitations
  • Feature requests that added complexity without improving confidence were deprioritized

These trade-offs helped maintain clarity, trust, and scalability.

Visual Design & Accessibility

The visual language focused on:

  • High contrast and outdoor legibility
  • Calm, confidence-building color usage
  • Consistent components across screens

Every UI decision supported comprehension first, aesthetics second.

Impact

After launch:

  • Engagement with ride summaries increased
  • Riders reported clearer understanding of vehicle behavior
  • Confusion around charging and range decreased
  • The app became a central part of the ownership experience

More importantly, the product established a foundation for future connected features.

What I’d Do Next

  • Personalize insights based on riding behavior
  • Introduce proactive alerts and recommendations
  • Expand integrations across the mobility ecosystem

Challenges and Reflections

One of the primary challenges in designing Yatri Hub was balancing the need for rich, data-heavy functionality with a clean and intuitive user experience. Riders wanted access to detailed bike statistics, ride history, and system alerts, but presenting too much information at once risked overwhelming users—especially while riding. This pushed me to prioritize information hierarchy, progressive disclosure, and contextual surfaces so that critical information was always accessible without cognitive overload.

Working on Yatri Hub significantly shaped my approach to product design. I learned how critical it is to design within real constraints, hardware limitations, safety considerations, and technical dependencies while still advocating for user needs. The project strengthened my ability to work cross-functionally, make informed design trade-offs, and think beyond screens to the broader ecosystem in which a product lives. Most importantly, it reaffirmed my passion for creating seamless interactions between humans and connected devices, especially in mobility-driven experiences.
